about.title: Lemon Grove Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Lemon Grove residents rely on a mix of local clinics and larger San Diego County hospital systems for care, and most visits go the way they should. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication is mismanaged, the effects can follow a patient for years. California law gives injured patients a path to accountability, though medical malpractice cases carry strict rules that don't apply to ordinary injury claims — including a short filing window, a required pre-suit notice, and a cap on certain damages. A bad medical outcome by itself doesn't prove negligence occurred; a qualified medical expert typically has to review the case and confirm the care fell below an accepted standard. Our team reviews medical records, explains the MICRA framework, and helps determine whether a claim is worth pursuing.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a California Medical Malpractice Claim

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims within one year of discovering the harm, and no later than three years after the injury itself, so acting promptly matters.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law usually requires giving the healthcare provider 90 days' written notice, which affects how and when a claim can move forward.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone isn't enough to prove malpractice, a qualified medical expert typically must confirm that the care fell short of the accepted standard.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Lemon Grove?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA framework, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it happened. These deadlines are strict, so it helps to have records reviewed early. We can look at your specific timeline and explain how it applies.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. Medicine involves risk, and an unfortunate result doesn't by itself mean a provider was negligent. California requires a qualified medical expert to review the care and confirm it fell below the accepted standard before a claim can move forward.

items.question: Does Lemon Grove have local hospitals involved in these claims?
items.answer: Lemon Grove residents typically receive care through nearby San Diego County medical facilities and clinics, and claims can involve any provider — from a local urgent care to a larger hospital system. We can help identify which providers may be involved in your specific situation.

items.question: How does this work?
items.answer: We review your case for free and help you understand your rights under California medical malpractice law. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.
